content.text: I could only see part of `UsersService.create`, so this diagnosis is inferred. I haven't confirmed it against the code that was cut off.

candidates.explanation: The login error `needLoginViaProvider:google` means the saved user has `provider` set to `google`. `AuthService.register` passes no provider, so `UsersService.create` must pick the default. The retrieved snippet cuts off before the part that builds the user and sets `provider`. The likely defect is there: the default should be `createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email`, but it appears to fall back to `google` (or another wrong value). Email-registered users are then stored with the wrong provider, and `validateLogin` rejects them.

`register` spreads the whole `dto` into `usersService.create` and never sets `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email`. It relies entirely on a default in `UsersService.create`, and it could pass through an unwanted `provider` value from the request body. Setting the provider explicitly here would remove that risk.

This is where the 422 `needLoginViaProvider:<provider>` is raised, because `user.provider !== AuthProvidersEnum.email`. The check itself is correct. It only reports the wrong provider that was stored at registration.

fix.description: In `UsersService.create`, make the saved user's provider default to `AuthProvidersEnum.email` (`provider: createUserDto.provider ?? AuthProvidersEnum.email`) instead of `google`. Also set `provider: AuthProvidersEnum.email` explicitly in `AuthService.register`, after the `...dto` spread.
